cues: Oxaloacetate becomes malate, which moves into the bundle sheath.
There it releases its carbon dioxide, building a concentration ten to twenty times that of air, right around RuBisCO.
Flooded with carbon dioxide, RuBisCO hardly ever grabs oxygen.
